# implement.py parent misclassifies soft-deleted children

## Problem
`implement.py parent <parent-id>` treats a child whose `deletedBy` is set (soft-deleted; `status` remains `open`) as implementable. `_classify_child` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` only checks `status` against `TERMINAL_STATUSES` ({in_review, completed, done, deleted}); it never inspects `deletedBy`. As a result `phase_parent` calls `phase_start` on the soft-deleted child, creates a bogus worktree/branch, claims the item `in_progress`, and stops the chain instead of advancing the parent.

## Reproduction
`wl delete <child>` on a child of an epic sets `deletedBy` but leaves `status: open` (verified with SA-0MUD5SYC0002SX5X / SA-0MUD5U06J009V0EK, both `deletedBy: plan`). Running `implement.py parent SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0` then started a worktree for SA-0MUD5SYC0002SX5X and set it `in-progress`, even though both real children were `completed`.

## Expected
A child with `deletedBy` set must be treated as terminal (`skip-terminal`): never claimed, never given a worktree, and never allowed to block parent advancement.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_classify_child` treats `deletedBy` (non-empty) as terminal regardless of `status`.
- [ ] `phase_parent` advances a parent whose only non-terminal statuses are soft-deleted children.
- [ ] Soft-deleted children count as terminal when gating in-chain blockers, so a child blocked only by a soft-deleted sibling is still startable (terminal determination must be consistent with `_classify_child`, not status-only).
- [ ] Regression test: a soft-deleted child is skipped and the parent advances.

## Plan: changelog
- 2026-10-07 — plan skill auto-complete path (effort Extra Small / risk Low, approval gate not warranted): added AC3 so the terminal determination used for in-chain blocker gating matches `_classify_child`; traced remaining ACs to the reported bug; no child work items created (below planning threshold).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
- None — the pre-check classified this item as below the planning threshold (Extra Small / Low), so no interview questions were asked. Seed intent was taken as authoritative from this work item's description (discovered-from SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MR12G1NH0097Z59** – Clarify stage vs status lifecycle in AGENTS.md and implement skill (completed)
- **SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E** – [CRITICAL] Audit runner has circular dependency — child audit verdict blocks parent regardless of stage (completed)
- **SA-0MSHZ08OE0033049** – Remove AMPA documentation (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mua4q431008hih0, acceptance, advances, allowed, block (+60 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mua4q431008hih0, acceptance, block, branch, calls (+53 more)

# implement.py start fails to claim an open work item (invalid stage)

## Problem
With the installed Worklog CLI (wl 0.1.19), `wl update --stage in_progress` is rejected: valid stages are `idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_review, done`. `phase_start` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` claims via `StatusLifecycle.update_status(id, 'in_progress', stage='in_progress', ...)`, so claiming an `open` item fails outright:

```
wl ... update SA-... --status in_progress --json --stage in_progress --assignee Map
RuntimeError: Invalid stage "in_progress". Valid stages: idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_review, done.
```

When the item is already `in-progress`, only the stage update fails and `phase_start` logs a WARNING and proceeds. When the item is `open`, the combined update fails and `implement.py start` returns `success: false` — the normal (open -> in_progress) claim path is broken.

## Impact
Every `implement.py start` / `finish` on a freshly-opened item cannot claim it; agents must claim manually with a status-only update. Blocks the deterministic implement workflow.

## Expected
Claiming sets `status=in_progress` without an invalid stage (preserve the current stage or use a valid one). The StatusLifecycle claim path should not pass `stage='in_progress'` on a wl build that does not accept it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `implement.py start <id>` on an `open` item succeeds and sets `status=in_progress`.
- [ ] No `--stage in_progress` is sent to `wl` (or it is only sent when the installed wl supports it).
- [ ] Regression test asserts the claim path does not fail on a wl build whose stage enum excludes `in_progress`.
data.title: implement.py start cannot claim an open item: sets invalid stage in_progress (wl 0.1.19)
